'''Wendy Sadler''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|MBE}} <small>[[Fellow of the Institute of Physics|FInstP]] [[Advance HE|FHEA]] [[Learned Society of Wales|FLSW]]</small> is a British [[science communication|science communicator]] and lecturer at [[Cardiff University]]. She is the founding director of [[Science Made Simple]], which focuses on engaging audiences with the physical sciences. Her areas of interest include inspiring the next generation of scientists, engineers and communicators; [[Women in STEM fields|women in STEM]]; and making [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]] subjects accessible to diverse audiences.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=http://www.sciencemadesimple.co.uk/about/staff/wendy-sadler|title=Wendy Sadler -|work=science made simple|access-date=2018-10-08|language=en-US|archive-date=15 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181215133044/http://www.sciencemadesimple.co.uk/about/staff/wendy-sadler|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Sadler was born in 1972 and grew up in [[Wombourne]], England, where she went to [[Ounsdale High School]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.compassmr.co.uk/news/science-advocate-receives-mbe-queens-birthday-honours/|title=Science advocate receives MBE in Queen's birthday honours - Compass Media Relations|date=2017-06-19|work=Compass Media Relations|access-date=2017-12-28|language=en-US}}</ref> She attended [[Cardiff University]] and gained a BSc in physics and music in 1994.<ref>{{cite web |last1=House |first1=McKenzie |title=Wendy Sadler |url=https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/people/view/913831-sadler-wendy |website=Cardiff University |language=en}}</ref> She gained an MSc in science communication at the Open University,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/Wendy-Sadler/e/B001K8QG3G|title=Amazon.co.uk: Wendy Sadler: Books, Biography, Blogs, Audiobooks, Kindle|website=www.amazon.co.uk|access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref> where her dissertation assessed the long-term impact of science demonstration shows.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sciencemadesimple.co.uk/about/research_evaluation|title=Research and Evaluation -|work=science made simple|access-date=2017-12-28|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Career==
Sadler started her career at [[Techniquest]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/wales-news/rugby-pundit-jonathan-davies-adds-1908309|title=Rugby pundit Jonathan Davies adds to his honours|last=Turner|first=Robin|date=2010-07-15|work=walesonline|access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://speakingofscience.juliegould.net/science-communication/speaking-to-wendy-sadler/|title=Speaking to...Wendy Sadler - Speaking of Science |date=2012-11-19|work=Speaking of Science|access-date=2017-12-28|language=en-US}}</ref>

She began her communications career by creating the non-verbal theatre show called The Experimentrics, which mixed physical theatre and live science demonstrations to create "a world of wordless mystery and fun".<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.experimentrics.co.uk/about/|title=About - The Experimentrics|work=The Experimentrics|access-date=2017-12-28|language=en-US}}</ref> She is now a LAMDA accredited public speaker and [[fellow of the Royal Society]] of the Arts who has appeared on ITV Wales, BBC Radio and the Edinburgh Fringe Festival to discuss the importance of STEM education<ref>{{Citation|last=ScienceMadeSimpleUK|title=Wendy Sadler on Why We Need Science In Schools - The Wales Report, BBC|date=2013-07-03|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=duyrZqBsCQM|access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Wendy Sadler|title=Wendy on Alan Titchmarsh show 26th Oct|date=2012-04-07|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dDdZ_yukdKU|access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Ignite Cardiff|title=Science Vs Ghosts (Ignite Cardiff 14 - Episode 2 - Wendy Sadler)|date=2013-12-19|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q_EaHC2O0pw|access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/radio4/science/leadingedge_20050310.shtml|title=BBC - Radio 4 - Leading Edge 10/03/2005|last=BBC|website=www.bbc.co.uk|language=en|access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-wales-25085193|title=Silent science show targets children|date=2013-11-25|work=BBC News|access-date=2017-12-28|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/news/view/34706-inspiring-young-scientists|title=Inspiring young scientists|work=News|access-date=2017-12-28|language=en}}</ref>

== Public engagement ==
Sadler has published 19 books for children.<ref name=":0" />

In 2010 Sadler gave a TEDxCardiff talk titled, "Music and the Machine".<ref>{{Citation|last=TEDx Talks|title=TEDxCardiff - Wendy Sadler - Music and the Machine|date=2010-06-13|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d15EdTBjv4k|access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref>

== Science Made Simple ==
Sadler set up Science Made Simple (SMS) in 2002 with the mission to inspire the next generation of scientists and engineers.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://leadingwalesawards.co.uk/social-enterprse-2015/|title=Social Enterprise 2015|website= Leading Wales Awards 2017|language=en-US|access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref> At the time, Sadler was an IOP schools lecturer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.iop.org/news/17/june/page_69622.html|title=Five IOP members receive Queen's Birthday Honours|last=Physics|first=Institute of|website=www.iop.org|language=en-GB|access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref> SMS develops and presents interactive performances that travel to schools and festivals across the world.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cardiffmet.ac.uk/news/Pages/20Twenty-Graduate-named-Winner-at-Leading-Wales-Awards-2015.aspx|title=20Twenty Graduate named Winner at Leading Wales Awards 2015|website=[[Cardiff Metropolitan University]]|language=en|access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref> They have produced shows, contributed to science television, radio programmes, and children's books, trained scientists and acted as consultants on UK research councils.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.iop.org/interactions/archive/INTApr07totalWeb.pdf|title=Newsmakers|work=Interactions: The Newspaper of The Physics Community|access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref> In 2013, she received national media coverage for their tour of UK primary schools following a sell-out run at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.astro.cf.ac.uk/newsandevents/?page=news_detail&news=0236|title=News|website=www.astro.cf.ac.uk|access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref> SMS is also part of a multimillion-pound EU project investigating the use of performance as a tool to engage young people with science and society issues.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sciencemadesimple.co.uk/training/perform-project|title=The EU funded PERFORM Project -|work=science made simple|access-date=2017-12-28|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Work with the Welsh Government ==
Sadler is a lecturer and schools' liaison officer at Cardiff University.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/people/view/913831-sadler-wendy|title=Wendy Sadler|work=People|access-date=2017-12-28|language=en}}</ref> She is concerned about the state of science education in Wales.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://soapboxscience.org/is-wales-in-a-science-education-crisis/|title=Is Wales in a science-education crisis? - SoapboxScience|date=2015-04-28|work=SoapboxScience|access-date=2017-12-28|language=en-US}}</ref>

She is a former member of the Science Advisory Council for Wales.<ref>[https://www. perform-research.eu/about/partners/sciencemadesimple/]</ref> She chaired and co-authored the Task and Finish report on STEM engagement in Wales for the National Science Academy<ref>{{Cite web |url= https://gov.wales/topics/science-and-technology/science/national-science-academy/?lang=en |title=Welsh Government {{!}} National Science Academy |website= gov.wales |language=EN |access-date=2018-10-08}}</ref> and was involved in the writing of the Talented Women for a Successful Wales<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gov.wales/docs/det/report/160308-women-in-science-en.pdf|title=Talented Women for a Successful Wales}}</ref> report.<ref name=":2" />
